pm_exper_user_2354_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I keep myself from obsessing over every little decoration decision and actually finish planning my event?
pm_exper_user_2354_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Treat the event like a live baseball game sketch — you don’t have time to capture every stitch on a jersey, just the energy and essentials. Let go of perfecting tiny décor choices and focus on the atmosphere you want guests to feel, just like you would with the mood of a finished piece.
(b) Think of your event plan the way you’d decide on a composition for your thesis illustrations — once the main structure feels strong, stop re-sketching the little details. You can set a cut-off date for decoration tweaks so you don’t get trapped in the same perfectionist loop that’s slowed your art projects.
(c) Think of your event plan like a quick draft — once the core elements are in place, avoid tinkering endlessly with minor details. Set a firm decision deadline for décor so you can focus on creating a great overall experience instead of chasing impossible perfection.
(d) Give yourself the same boundaries you wish you had during thesis revisions: lock in your decoration choices after one or two review passes. That way you channel your creative energy into execution instead of endlessly reworking details like you tend to with your artwork.
